judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the TICKETMASTER accordion toggle: div.qna-item__button that holds the h3 and the chevron and opens the hidden qna-item__content panel. The CDP capture records it with role generic, no name, focusable, and click and keydown listeners attached to it, so the claim holds for the capture. One caveat: CDP's focusable flag would also be set by tabindex=-1, but the keydown listener points to intended keyboard use. I looked for something that would make it pass and found none. It has no role, no aria-expanded and no name, and the item holds no native button or link (the h3 is plain text). That is F59, and the expanded/collapsed state isn't exposed either. It would still fail 4.1.2 even if it were not in the tab order. The screenshot shows the fully styled page, with nothing to suggest a bot-only version. The live page returns 403 to curl, and WebFetch gives text only. It still shows the four accordion sections, but I could not compare the markup or roles, so captureDiffers is cannot_tell. The claim names the actual failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the chevron icon (angle-down-white.svg, alt "angle down white") inside the CAREERS accordion toggle. The crop the model saw, and the screenshot, show exactly that: a white down-pointing angle on dark navy. So the claim that the alternative describes something the image does not show is false of the capture. WebFetch shows the live page carries the same alt on the same icons. The image does fail 1.1.1, but for a different reason. The alt is the file name restated, describing how the icon looks (F30). It should be null if the icon is decorative (F38), or should convey the expand function, which the toggle doesn't expose anywhere. The claim points at a mismatch with the picture, not at that, so this is a false positive. The model had the crop and judged it wrongly.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the full-width background photo (img.subscribe__bg) behind the newsletter section: a packed auditorium and a lit stage. Its alt is "subscribe". It is not inside the 'Sign me up' link, which is a separate anchor in the form. The heading, intro text and button are HTML laid over the photo, and their text matches the snapshot. Read as informative, "subscribe" doesn't describe it. Either way, the fault is the label used as its alternative, which is what the claim points at, so this is a true positive.
